correctness.rationale: At p=65537 (prime by exact trial division), every a=46256,...,46268 has a^16384 in {256,65281} and its square equals -1 mod p; thus a^32768=-1 and a has exact order 2^16=p-1, since the ambient prime-field multiplicative group is of order 2^16. Odd-degree M_m=(p^m-1)/(p-1) is odd; therefore the same a has order p-1<q-1, so nonprimitive, and a^((q-1)/2)=(-1)^M_m=-1, so nonsquare. For odd prime degrees ell, the odd repunit M_ell has only prime divisors r with ord_r(p)=ell and thus r≡1 mod ell; factoring q-1=2^16 M_ell gives theta=1/2∏(1-1/r). Since their count s<ell logp/log(ell+1), 0<1/2-theta<ell logp/[2(ell+1)log(ell+1)]→0. For ANY odd finite field theta≤1/2 and equality eliminates all NSNP elements; hence sharp unattained supremum 1/2 for each 3≤k≤13. Boundaries: m is any odd integer≥3 for the block; ell ranges only odd rational primes for convergence; characteristic p>13 ensures distinct additive constants; m=1 not included.
residual_risks: The analytic bound is crude for small ell, but the asymptotic conclusion is valid as ell grows.
The theorem does not determine max possible consecutive NSNP length in all finite fields, nor the distribution of such blocks, nor a rate along all odd composite degrees.
No Lean formalization or outside expert attestation, which is not needed for this independently reconstructed argument.

value.rationale: The invariant theta_q and NSNP run-existence threshold are natural in finite-field multiplicative combinatorics. The theorem supplies a sharp but unattained HIGH-density extremum for 11 block lengths 3 through 13, showing a vanishing ambient fraction of NSNPs can retain a fixed run of 13; it clarifies the conceptual distinction between universal low-density guarantees and extremal high-density counterexamples. The finite witness is already available in an established primitive-root table, so the contribution is the uniform odd-extension persistence and sharp infinite-family density boundary, not a new primality table, novel algorithm or generic textbook lemma. The independently checked maximum length 13 in this PARTICULAR prime field motivates the natural cutoff; no maximality across all fields is asserted. This is an exact self-contained extremal result, not a claim to solve general longest-run growth.
residual_risks: The finite base witness and lifting technique are elementary/known ingredients; the value judgment depends on the distinct extremal synthesis, not independent novelty of each component.
No bound on maximal NSNP run length across arbitrary fields and no claim of optimized density convergence rate.
